title: The Opening of the Season
sceneText:
The hunting ground is open country. The smell of the pine camp mixed with dung and leather. The Duke’s banner hangs slack; there is not enough autumn wind today to hold it.

The nobility and their stewards are spread out between the fires and the tents. Baron Henk is at the centre of it, laughing among a group of hunters he knows. Marguerite sits in a folding chair with a half-closed book in her hand, and her eyes are not on it.

Further off, a party is mounting up. There are many more of them than there are here, and they are turned out differently: dark riding dress all matching, and the same device on the tack. Somebody in the middle of that party — at this distance all you can see is that she is laughing.

Somebody beside her points towards the tree line, and she nods. The whole party begins to move.

From start to finish nobody looks over this way.

The Duke’s party goes. You watched for less than a minute.

Henk sees you and waves.

“Maplegate. You came.” He puts a hand on your shoulder. “Hartmann was always finding reasons those last few years. We had all assumed that estate was done with hunting for good.”

He steers you towards the fire.

Halfway there a man in a dark green coat comes round from behind a tent with a sheet of paper covered in lines. He is giving instructions to two men behind him as he walks, and they are nodding.

Henk lets go of your shoulder.

“Vallant,” he calls. “Which side are we starting today?”

“South-east.” The man does not even look up. “That wind this morning has pressed the scent down low; the deer are below the slope. If you push from the north they will run out of the ground, and I have nobody set that side.”

Henk is blank for half a second, and then laughs. “As you say.”

variants.thierry_met:
“Again, then,” he says. “I did say I am in the woods two hundred days of the year. These five are inside that.”

He opens the sheet out a little further so that you can see it too.

“South-east today. If you are riding along, do not ride at the very front. That lot up there like to race, and when they race they do not watch the ground.”
variants.thierry_unmet: “Vallant. Forester, north district.” He folds the sheet away. “And you are the new steward at Maplegate.”

choices.text: Go with Henk to the fire

effects.logEntry: You went with Henk into the circle at the fire.

choices.resultText:
Henk takes you into the circle and names them one at a time. Two neighbouring landholders, a horse dealer up from Valehold, two stewards from other houses.

When he comes to you he says “the new steward at Maplegate”. He does not give your name, and he does not say that you are a foreigner.

“He has been here under a month,” Henk says, “and the books are straight already.”

You have no idea where he heard that.

Somebody in the circle asks where you are from. You tell them. Somebody says something and another man laughs. Not unkindly.

Half an hour later you notice that you are listening to them talk about other things — whose horses, whose land, this year’s prices. Nobody is asking you anything now.

This is more or less what it means to be caught when you fall.

choices.text: Pay your respects to Marguerite first

effects.logEntry: You went to pay your respects to Baroness Marguerite first.

choices.resultText:
You go over to the folding chair.

She does not look up. She closes the book first, and then looks at you.

“You came,” she says. “Nobody has come from Ludwig’s estate in two years.”

She glances towards the fire.

“Henk is delighted. Have you noticed that he asks once a year why nobody from Maplegate comes?”

She sets the book on her knees.

“He does not miss Hartmann. He dislikes having a place stand empty when he does not know who will end up sitting in it.”

choices.text: Stay where you are and watch how Thierry arranges it

effects.logEntry: You stayed where you were and watched the man in the green coat set out the day’s line.

choices.resultText:
You do not follow Henk straight away. You stay where you are and watch the man in the green coat.

He draws two more lines on the sheet, turns it round for the men beside him to see, says three sentences, and the two of them scatter to get on with it. The whole thing takes under a minute.

He looks up and sees you watching him.

choices.text: Find somewhere out of the way to stand

effects.logEntry: You found a place at the edge of the camp and stayed there.

choices.resultText:
You find a place at the edge of the camp, against an unhitched cart.

You can see the whole field from here. Henk at the centre, Marguerite in her chair, the man in the green coat giving instructions. Attendants carrying the wine jars. Somebody laughing.

You stand there about a quarter of an hour and nobody comes over.

This is not being slighted. Nobody has any obligation to come and find you today, and you walked to the edge yourself.

On the ride back at dusk Henk greeted you from the saddle, as warmly as he had in the morning.

But you heard nothing at all the whole afternoon.
